body_excerpt:
Real-time mutexes in the Linux kernel implement priority inheritance, which requires walking a chain of waiting tasks whenever a waiter's priority changes. During removal of a waiter, the waiter structure is released while still linked into that chain, so a subsequent chain walk dereferences freed memory. The path is reachable from user space through priority-inheritance futexes, which any local process can use via standard threading library mutex attributes.
